To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the most common behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) in patients with dementia are agitation, aggression and psychosis, (2) BPSD have a negative impact on caregivers and patients and are associated with increased mortality in dementia, (3) non-pharmacologic approaches should be the first line of intervention, (4) antipsychotics are effective in reducing BPSD but have serious adverse effects, (5) cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are effective

the use of the following medications is not recommended: antipsychotics, antiepileptic agents, antidepressants, and cholinesterase inhibitors for the treatment of behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD).
the use of a combination of pharmacological and nonpharmacological interventions is the most effective way to treat behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and better methods for the treatment of dementia, particularly Alzheimer's disease.
the study of the effects of different types of social interactions on the behaviour and well‐being of elderly residents.
understanding the role of the environment and its impact on the behavior of individuals with dementia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of antipsychotic medication in people with dementia and behavioural problems should be considered only as a last resort, after other non‐pharmacotherapies have been tried and failed.
the treatment of behavioural problems in people with dementia is complex.
the treatment of behavioural disturbances in dementia is complex and requires an individual approach to each patient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are no specific drugs for behavioural disturbances in dementia, but there is an array of drugs that may be used in a rational manner to achieve a satisfactory result.
the treatment of behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia is challenging and requires careful consideration of a number of factors.
the use of antipsychotics for the treatment of behavioral and psychological symptoms in dementia should be avoided.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the treatment of behavioural symptoms of dementia is complex and requires a multidisciplinary approach.
the treatment of behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) should be based on an individualized approach.
there is no single approach that works in all cases.
